analyst_view.overall: Early view: Leipzig have won all five home league games with a 23-2 goal difference under Martín Demichelis. Mainz are an odd case among the struggling sides, poor at home but strong away (nine of their ten points on the road), though they lost four of their last five in all competitions before the break.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. I lean higher: Leipzig average more than four goals a game at home and Mainz have scored most of their goals away, through Phillip Tietz, Sheraldo Becker and Benedict Hollerbach. Mainz's defence conceded nine in three games in late October.

corners.text: The site expects 9.8 corners. Leipzig dominate the ball at home (about 65% against Augsburg) but often score before corners pile up, and Mainz counter rather than cross. I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. Urs Fischer has described Mainz's style as 'slightly nasty' and Stefan Posch was sent off at Elversberg, so I lean slightly higher, even though Leipzig themselves are rarely booked.

shots.text: The site has 28.9 shots. That fits a dominant Leipzig at home and a Mainz side that gets chances on the break, so I stay level.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.4 on target. In line with my goals view I lean slightly higher: Leipzig's attack (Rômulo, Christopher Nkunku, Brajan Gruda) has been ruthless at home, scoring five against Augsburg.
